notebook:
PLAN: Step 1 map sharp C4/C5 split and costs; step 2 add high-value C5+ separation branches; step 3 add light-product branches only if profitable; step 4 tune stages/reflux and copy stronger team designs.
First column targets ethane-through-butane overhead and C5+ bottoms. Moderate settings should reveal separation quality and energy/capital scale before committing solves.

note: Build the high-value C4, C5, and C6-paraffin blend backbone, with a sharper, less reboiled root cut.
notebook:
PLAN: Build blend backbone: root C4/C5, T C3/C4, B C5/C6+, BB C6 paraffins/heavies; then add naphthene and heavy pure-product branches and tune costs.
Root at 70/4/4 cost $261M and cut too deep (1260 vs ideal 864 mol/s). Reduce reboil to 2.0. Blends avoid difficult isomer splits: C4 ~$195M, C5 ~$610M, C6 paraffin ~$1250M potential. BB is hardest (n-hexane/MCP only 3 K apart), so use 70 stages and reflux 5 initially.

note: Sharpen the C5/C6 split and add a small ethane/C3 column so all three light and middle blends can sell.
notebook:
PLAN: Build blend backbone: root C4/C5, T C3/C4, B C5/C6+, BB C6 paraffins/heavies; then add naphthene and heavy pure-product branches and tune costs. Step: sharpen B and add ethane/C3 splitter.
Root gives useful C4 blend. T bottoms already sell ($172.5M). TT cannot reach 95% C3 directly because ethane is lighter; add TT to reject ethane. B currently passes ~360 mol/s C6 into C5 tops: reduce boil-up 2.5->1.0 and raise reflux. BB feed will then contain all C6 paraffins, improving blend purity; reduce boil-up to keep heptane+ out. C6 potential ~$1B/yr, C5 ~$610M.

note: Increase separation in the two high-value blend columns while setting intermediate cut rates to recover C5 and C6 without their heavier neighbors.
notebook:
PLAN: Build blend backbone: root C4/C5, T C3/C4, B C5/C6+, BB C6 paraffins/heavies; then add naphthene and heavy pure-product branches and tune costs. Step: make B and BB actually hit 95% blend specs.
C4 and C3 branches sell $226M. Prior low boil-up stranded C5/C6 in bottoms; agent-7's high boil-up recovered them but with contamination. Increase both middle columns to 90 stages/RR6, with B boil2.5 for a C5 cut and BB boil5 to recover all C6 paraffins. Their combined blend upside is about $1.75B/yr, justifying substantial separation cost. If purities remain short, tune cut rates before adding more branches.

note: Push both near-spec blend columns decisively above 95%; their combined $1.44B revenue upside justifies this test, after which severity can be reduced.
notebook:
PLAN: Build blend backbone: root C4/C5, T C3/C4, B C5/C6+, BB C6 paraffins/heavies; then add naphthene and heavy pure-product branches and tune costs. Step: make B and BB actually hit 95% blend specs.
C4 and C3 branches sell $226M. B at 90/RR6/boil2.5 gave C5 85%; BB at 90/RR6/boil5 gave C6 paraffin 89%. These are close enough that a decisive reflux/stage increase should unlock $565M+$875M, still profitable despite expensive columns. Test B 120/RR10/boil2.3 and BB 120/RR10/boil5. If specs hit, reduce severity to lower cost; otherwise change cut architecture.

note: Copy the proven R48 backbone by restoring B boil-up 3, then test the C6-paraffin split on its clean heavy feed.
notebook:
PLAN: Start from R48's profitable C3/C4/C5 backbone. Add a C6-paraffin/heavy split on the now-clean BB feed, tune it to 95%, then reduce column severity and add only clearly profitable heavy/naphthene branches. Step: test BB at 120 stages, RR10, boil5 on B boil3.
R48 earns 0.748 with B=120/10/3: C5 sells for $526M and costs $424M total. R44 shows that adding BB=90/8/4 gives only 84% C6 paraffin because ~15% C5 remains; with the clean R48 BB feed this contamination should largely vanish. My failed BB test used B boil2.3, so its result does not reject this split. C6-paraffin recovery is worth roughly $850M, enough to justify a substantial column if purity crosses 95%.

note: Sharpen the C5/C6 boundary with higher B reflux: this should remove the 15% residual C5 from BBT without risking BT's blend purity through higher boil-up.
notebook:
PLAN: Start from R48's profitable C3/C4/C5 backbone. Add a C6-paraffin/heavy split on the clean BB feed, tune it to 95%, then reduce column severity and add only clearly profitable heavy/naphthene branches. Step: increase B reflux to sharpen the C5/C6 split while retaining boil-up 3, so BB loses its residual C5 contamination.
R48/R54 earn ~0.749 with B=110-120/10/3: C5 sells for $526M and total cost is $424M. My BB=120/10/5 split gives BBT 84% C6 paraffin with 15% C5, so the split itself works but B leaves too much C5 behind. B boil-up 4 failed convergence and would also threaten BT's zero-margin 95% C5 purity. Higher B reflux should instead move residual C5 overhead without adding C6 to BT. C6-paraffin recovery is worth ~$682M, versus BB's $262M cost, so even a substantially more expensive B is worthwhile if both blends cross 95%.

note: Restore R61's proven 0.847 backbone and test a modestly higher C6-splitter boil-up to push its 94% paraffin cut above blend specification.
notebook:
PLAN: Restore the best proven four-column C3/C4/C5 plant (R61), then add one C6-paraffin splitter and tune its boil-up just enough to exceed 95%. If profitable, optimize its cost; otherwise retain R61 and test cheaper debottlenecking.
R61 earns 0.847 with B=110/9/3 and costs $418M; it strictly beats my high-reflux B experiment. R67 shows BB=120/10/5 on a nearly identical clean feed gives 94% C6 paraffin (6% n-hexane, 5% n-pentane), just below spec. On R61's slightly cleaner BB feed, increasing BB boil-up to 5.5 should drive more n-hexane overhead and cross 95%, unlocking roughly $680M revenue for about $260M cost. The C5 product must remain protected by using R61's proven B settings.

note: Adopt R77's proven 1.981 backbone and test the cheaper 110-stage, reflux-9 C5 splitter at the same boil-up 3.6, aiming to preserve blend grades while cutting cost.
notebook:

R77 proves B=120/10/3.6 plus BB=120/10/5 sells C5 and 96% C6 paraffin for $1573M at $704M cost. R61 shows B=110/9 works well at boil-up 3 and saves about $36M versus 120/10. Retaining R77's boil-up 3.6 should preserve C5 recovery and the low n-pentane leakage needed by BBT. C4/C3 settings are fixed and efficient. My failed BB=5.5 experiment used insufficient B boil-up and is superseded by R77.

note: Adopt R87's valid 2.102 backbone and trim the C6 splitter from 110 to 100 stages at unchanged ratios, seeking capital savings while retaining blend purity.
notebook:

Reducing BB by 10 stages at fixed ratios should save capital while retaining most separation. Reducing B stages/reflux at boil-up 3.6 caused nonconvergence, so do not repeat that. R81's higher B boil-up 3.7 worsened economics versus R87. C4/C3 settings are efficient and fixed.

note: Adopt R92's best backbone and test one further modest BB reflux reduction, seeking energy savings while retaining C6-paraffin blend grade.
notebook:

A further 0.5 reflux reduction may save energy, but BBT purity is close to 95%, so test one increment only. B=120/10/3.6 is essential to keep C5 out of BBT; 3.7 can raise C5 revenue but adds cost. Root and light columns are already efficient; heavy-stream side draw R96 was unsellable and lost revenue.

note: Trim the costly C5 splitter from 120 to 110 stages while holding its proven cut settings, seeking capital savings without losing either blend grade.
notebook:
